subject.title: feat(ios): Siri App Intent integration — native "Hey Siri, ask OpenClaw..." support

question: Should OpenClaw add a first-party iOS Siri/App Intent that sends dictated questions to an agent and returns spoken replies, and which auth/session boundary should it use?
rationale: The request is aligned with companion-app direction, but it adds a new voice/Shortcuts agent-execution surface where auth, session routing, confirmation, reply collection, and spoken output are product and security choices.

options.title: Approve design-gated native intent
options.body: Implement the Siri/App Intent only after maintainers choose credential storage, local confirmation, allowed agent/session routing, and spoken-reply behavior, then require real iOS device proof.

options.title: Limit scope to Talk Mode launch
options.body: Treat the open Action Button/Talk Mode work as the first-party shortcut surface and leave parameterized Siri questions out of scope for now.

options.title: Keep webhook workaround external
options.body: Decline first-party Siri agent execution until there is stronger demand or a safer extension API, leaving Shortcuts plus webhook as the supported workaround.

recommendation.title: Approve design-gated native intent
recommendation.body: Implement the Siri/App Intent only after maintainers choose credential storage, local confirmation, allowed agent/session routing, and spoken-reply behavior, then require real iOS device proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The current iOS gateway/session and security-boundary history points most strongly to this owner for the product/security decision.
